title: Microwidget legend and mini dashboard recipes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for a compact, reusable 'microwidget' pattern — tiny dashboard panels (140–240px height) intended for operator jump-boards, incident triage overlays, and high-density runbooks. Goal is to standardize legend/colour semantics, query cost limits, and a set of copy-paste panel recipes that teams can adopt with minimal instrumentation changes.

Why microwidgets?
- Many operators prefer compact, focused panels during incidents (less noise, faster pattern recognition).
- Large dashboards are expensive to render and query; microwidgets reduce query surface and make staging/embedding easier (slack-rich previews, runbook embeds).
- Promotes reuse across feature rollouts and model onboardings.

Design constraints (hard):
1) Query cost per microwidget <= 0.75 RU / refresh (approx) or a team budgeted equivalent.
2) Prefer pre-aggregated metrics / lightweight rate() or count() over subquery-heavy joins.
3) Panel refresh defaults: 30s for operator mode, 60s for on-call standby, 300s for executive/summary mode.
4) No raw token-level traces inside microwidget panels — show aggregated trace anchors only (link out to detailed trace viewer).

Legend & colour semantics (standardized):
- Good/healthy (green): P50 within SLO target and error rate < 0.1%
- Warning (amber): P95 approaches SLO (>= 75% of budget) OR error rate between 0.1% and 1%
- Degraded (red): P95 > SLO or error rate >= 1%
- Flaky (purple): high variance signals where P50/P95 diverge by > 3x (indicates cache/kv warmth issues)
- Neutral/Info (blue/grey): non-actionable telemetry (queue depth, background tasks)

Metric naming and aggregation rules (keep compact):
- Use short metric names with suffixes for aggregation:
  - inference.latency_ms.p50, inference.latency_ms.p95, inference.errors.per_1k
  - kvcache.warmth_pct, batch.size.avg
- Tagging: include tenant_id (if applicable), model_name, route_id. Dashboards should default to tenant_id=all but provide microwidget quick filters.

Microwidget recipes (copy-paste templates):
1) Mini latency sparkline + current state pill (ideal for runbook header)
  - Query (pseudo):
    - Line: p95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
    - Panel: sparkline of p95 (15m window), right-aligned status pill: current p95 value + colour per legend.
  - Purpose: quick answer — is p95 currently inside SLO?
  - Query cost notes: ensure bucket histograms are pre-aggregated; avoid 1s scrape windows.

2) Error-rate small stacked bar (recent intervals)
  - Query: sum(rate(inference_errors_total[1m])) by (error_type) normalized per 1000 requests.
  - Panel: 6× mini bars for last 6×1m buckets, with hover detail expanding to full graph.
  - Use-case: quick pattern recognition of new error classes.

3) Cache-warmth vs latency two-line micro (dual axis)
  - Query: kvcache.warmth_pct (15m avg) and p95 latency (15m p95) aligned.
  - Panel: small dual-axis trend, purple highlight if divergence threshold exceeded.
  - When to use: suspected cold-cache regressions during rollouts.

4) SLO burn gauge (compact donut)
  - Query: slo_burn = (error_budget_used / error_budget_total)
  - Panel: single-value gauge with 3-colour thresholds (green < 50%, amber 50–90%, red >= 90%).
  - Notes: backlinked to rollout page and 'why' metric.

5) Trace anchor + recent example link (text micro)
  - Show 1-2 trace IDs (most significant failures) with short summary (latency, route, model). Panel is mostly text with inline links to trace viewer.
  - Constraint: do not embed full spans (privacy & size concerns).

Embedding microwidgets in runbooks & Slack blocks:
- Each microwidget should expose: minimal PNG render endpoint (static snapshot), and a deep-link to the interactive dashboard and trace viewer.
- Slack previews should surface the status pill and top 2 hover details to reduce clicks.

Operational playbook (how to adopt across teams):
1) Instrumentation review: confirm metrics exist (p50/p95 histograms and error counters).
2) Create a microwidget fork in team's dashboard repo using the templates above (copy-only, no edits in global).
3) Run a cost simulation: render the microwidget across three time ranges (30d/7d/1d) and run query-cost estimator.
4) Stage: add to a 'mini-ops' dashboard and run with 60s refresh for 1 week. Collect operator feedback.
5) Promote and add to shared-runbook library with link and owner metadata.

Checklist before rolling microwidgets to PROD dashboards:
- [ ] Query cost OR RU estimates added to panel meta (value in RU or approximate cost).
- [ ] Owner assigned (oncall + team contact).
- [ ] Linked runbook present and validated (steps for escalation).
- [ ] Trace deep-links configured (tokenized and safe).
- [ ] Tagging consistent (model_name, route_id).

Troubleshooting heuristics (operator quick-hits):
- If p95 spikes but p50 stable -> suspect tail queues, large outlier requests, or cold-kv shards. Follow cache-warmth microwidget immediately.
- If both p50 and p95 shift up proportionally -> probable model-level regression or infra saturation. Scale/route policy checks.
- High error-rate but low latency -> input validation or recent config change. Check error bars microwidget for new error_type.

Future improvements (ideas to iterate on):
- Client-side widget concatenation: allow operators to assemble 4 microwidgets into a compact incident tile for quick sharing.
- Embed lite anomaly detectors in microwidgets (simple rolling z-score) to add a small flag without querying historical windows.
- Automatic mode switching: dashboard auto-switch from 300s -> 30s refresh when alert fires (requires rate-limiting of query surges).

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- Should microwidgets enforce tenant-level scrubbing by default (PII footprint)? (Pros: safety; Cons: loses context for tenant-specific problems)
- What is the acceptable RU budget per user session of an operator? Proposed: 5 RU / minute per operator session.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please check that colour thresholds align with your team's SLO definitions before adopting.
- Link feedback to JIRA-OBS-412 (linked above).

Quick links:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood/company/obs-miniwidgets-catalog
- Example dashboard repo: github.com/redwood/observability/dashboards/tree/miniwidgets
- Related runbook: linked_artifacts JIRA-OBS-412

---
Author notes: sketchy RHS queries are pseudocode — teams must replace histogram_quantile calls with their Prometheus-compatible variants or telemetry provider equivalents. This doc intentionally keeps examples lightweight so people can copy small panels into feature dashboards quickly.
